claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Live CLI validation: this run's runner reports `claude --version` as `2.1.273 (Claude Code)`, matching the target exactly (the previous run, on 2026-09-15, was one release behind the runner's live CLI and had to fall back to a changelog-based review for the 2.1.271/2.1.272 delta — see the 2.1.258 precedent in platform-targets.md for that distinction). `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.272 to **2.1.273** together (no divergence). Reviewed the full published 2.1.273 changelog entry line by line for catalog surface. Every New-Features line in 2.1.273 (gateway hint request headers, an MCP-disconnect notification, forking a `--remote-control` session, Remote Control fast mode, `/config` panel mouse support, `claude self-hosted-runner --drain-marker-file`, per-command `allowed_domains` on Bash/PowerShell/Monitor in auto mode, `omitClaudeMd`, `--accept-command <sha256>`, the `modelPricing`/gateway `pricing` multiplier, and the Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway spinner tip) restates or extends items already reviewed in the 2.1.271 delta (see the `-2.1.271` suffixed `features_adopted` entry below) — `--accept-command <sha256>` was already adopted and documented there, and the rest were already checked and found not applicable to this personal, manifest-only catalog (no managed MCP config, no custom/plugin subagents, no Bash permission-rule examples, no gateway/chargeback pricing); nothing changed on a second look. None of the 2.1.273 Bug Fixes, Improvements, or Changes entries touch marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading behavior either — checked directly for the closest candidates: the fix for skills synced from claude.ai staying available after an org turns Skills off (this catalog's own skill is a plain repo skill, never cloud-synced, matching the existing 2.1.269 `anthropic-skills:<name>` finding); `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`/`deniedMcpServers`/`disableClaudeAiConnectors` under MDM (no managed settings configured for this personal catalog); and 'sign-in with a Claude account also requests access to your claude.ai plugins' (an account-scope change with no marketplace-manifest or install-flow effect on this catalog). Platform-Specific (VSCode/Windows/web/Claude Tag/Code Review) entries are all host/editor/chat-app-side with zero surface here. `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` (piped through `scripts/report-skill-validation.py`) and a full `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`, 3 plugins in sync, no drift) both passed clean against the live 2.1.273 CLI. Nothing to adopt beyond the version bump — the prior 2.1.271 review (`--accept-command <sha256>`, documented) and 2.1.272 (pure compatibility bump) remain the most recent substantive and itemized deltas respectively; full per-version history remains in the install guide's per-version sections.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download API (3.21.13, 2026-09-18) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-10 Projects; prior Self-Hosted Machines 2026-09-02); CLI changelog through 2026-08-26 (agent persist); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
